subtopic: SASKATCHEWAN

speechtext:
Regina, December 6, 1949
Hon. Douglas C. Abbott,
Minister of Finance,
Ottawa, Ontario.
Dear Mr. Abbott:
Re rent control
I wish to thank you for your letter of December 2.
My letter to you of November 16 set out the position of the Saskatchewan government, namely:
(1)	That the order permitting rent increases on December 15 should be made inoperative in this province.
(2)	That Saskatchewan was prepared to enter the rent control field.
(3)	That we desired an assurance that you had jurisdiction to place Saskatchewan in the field while it was still occupied by the dominion. We requested a supreme court reference to determine your jurisdiction in this respect.
Your last letter, we take it, is a definite refusal to refer the question to the supreme court. We regret this, and cannot agree with you that such a reference is "undesirable" or that it "might confuse the main issue". With respect, we doubt if the learned members of the supreme court would be confused by submitting a second question arising out of the same subject matter as the first.
We also find it difficult to agree that "all that can be asked is a hypothetical question" because there is no provincial legislation to be referred. The question we desire answered is not one of provincial but of dominion jurisdiction.
You have been informing the provinces for a year that if they or any of them expressed a willingness to take over rent control you would put them in the field, tomorrow, I believe was the expression used. It is to obtain a ruling placing beyond doubt your power to carry out your undertaking and put a single province in the field that we requested a reference to the supreme court.
Your argument that a reference to determine the legal position of landlords and tenants of Saskatchewan might delay a decision on the main issue comes strangely from yourself, as you are already on record as holding the opinion that the question can be answered only in one way as there is no reasonable doubt of the legal position. Surely if you are correct in your view the supreme court justices will be able to reach that decision as quickly as your law officers did.
Your refusal, however, to have the point passed on must be accepted as law; we cannot change it.
In the opinion of our government the recent order permitting heavy increases in rents, straight across the board, without consideration of the merits of individual cases is so inequitable and iniquitous that we must submit to your terms to have it annulled in Saskatchewan no matter how arbitrary we think those terms are.
Saskatchewan will therefore consent to the two orders being passed; one making the recent rent increases inoperative in Saskatchewan and the other making all federal rental regulations inoperative in Saskatchewan from and after April 1, 1950.
This consent is given because of the assurance of your law officers that the second order will be so drawn as to enable Saskatchewan to pass valid legislation respecting rent control.
The consent is conditional, however, on your assurance that if your law officers are at a later date proven wrong and it is held by the courts that we cannot enter the field you will take the necessary steps to put Saskatchewan back under federal controls. Inadequate as we think your regulations are we cannot permit a situation to arise where Saskatchewan will have no rental controls at all.
We agree that an amendment to the Continuation of Transitional Measures Act is advisable but do not think the amendment proposed in your letter is the appropriate one. We desire an amendment that will, inasmuch as dominion legislation can do it, put beyond question the power of the governor in council by executive action to confer legislative jurisdiction respecting rent control on one province or on any number less than all. We do not wish to confuse the main issue, however, and think the

Appendix
form of the amendment can be worked out later. We believe It should follow the general lines of the suggestions made in the house the other night by your colleague, Mr. Garson.
At a later date we intend to request you to renew your oifer to pay the cost of provincial rent control. This would appear to be only fair and reasonable, if, for instance, Saskatchewan alone undertakes the work and relieves you of an item of expense you are incurring in the other provinces where rent control is left with the dominion.
It will therefore be in order for you to proceed with the two orders, on giving us the assurance that in the event of the courts finding that Saskatchewan control legislation is beyond our jurisdiction you will put Saskatchewan back under federal controls if any are in force at that time.
Yours sincerely,
T. C. Douglas

Ottawa, December 8, 1949
Hon. T. C. Douglas,
Premier of Saskatchewan,
Regina, Saskatchewan.
My dear Premier:
Thank you for your letter of December 6, which I have discussed today with my colleagues in the government.
Pursuant to your request and in accordance with the announced policy of the government, the wartime prices and trade board is today issuing an order which makes orders 813 and 814 of the board inoperative in Saskatchewan and revokes the wartime leasehold regulations in their entirety as they apply to Saskatchewan as from April 1, 1950.
If it is conclusively determined by the courts that legislation enacted by the legislature of Saskatchewan, with respect to landlord and tenant relationships, is invalid because and only because regulations of the federal government remain in effect elsewhere in Canada, the federal government will take the necessary steps to put Saskatchewan back under then existing rental controls.
We shall be prepared to consider a request that the federal government pay the cost of administering provincial rent control in Saskatchewan for a period not exceeding one year. You will understand, of course, that any agreement would be subject to approval by parliament.
Yours very truly,

speechtext:
Quebec, December 7. 1949
Hon. D. C. Abbott,
Minister of Finance,
Ottawa.
Mr. Minister of Finance:
Today, at our first meeting held since Wednesday last, the members of the executive council of the province took cognizance of your letter dated December 2, delivered at my office on the 5th of the same month, concerning federal rent control.
We reiterate each and every one of the statements contained in the letters which we wrote to you on the subject, particularly the two following paragraphs of our letter of November 30 last:
"Far from offering to the province the full exercise of its rights in this field, the federal government continues to render the full exercise thereof practically impossible.
"We respectfully suggest to the federal government that it should modify its attitude and make it consistent with the rights of the provinces and with the rights of the people concerned. By removing, as you could easily do, the further and grave difficulties which you have added to the difficulties inherent in the problem, you would help solve the question rather than make it more complicated and more difficult. As to the present government of the province of Quebec, it is always ready to assume its responsibilities, but it desires that the federal government assume its own without any further delay."
Yours sincerely,
M. L. Duplessis
MINISTER OF FINANCE Canada
